title: U.S. House · Georgia's 13th District
area: South metro Atlanta, including Clayton County and parts of south Fulton and south DeKalb counties.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent David Scott (D) is not on the May 2026 primary or November general-election ballot. Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball rate the general election Solid/Safe Democratic.

candidates.name: Jasmine Clark
candidates.currentRole: Member, Georgia House of Representatives, District 108 (since 2019)

summary.text: Jasmine Clark is the Democratic nominee in Georgia's 13th District, an open seat. A microbiologist who teaches at Emory University's nursing school, she has represented Georgia House District 108 since 2019 after defeating a Republican incumbent in 2018. She is running for Congress on a platform her campaign describes as defending healthcare, science-based policy, and democratic institutions.

background.text: Born in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1982; Wikipedia lists a Bachelor of Science from the University of Tennessee.
Earned a Ph.D. in microbiology from Emory University.

Works as a scientist and instructor at Emory University's Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing; directed the 2017 March for Science in Atlanta and has worked with the Georgia Alliance for Social Justice.
Won Georgia House District 108 on November 6, 2018, defeating incumbent Republican Clay Cox; took office January 14, 2019. Her campaign website says she flipped a long-held Republican seat.

Won re-election to the Georgia House in 2020, 2022, and 2024. Her committee assignments in the 2025-2026 session include Banks and Banking, Budget and Fiscal Affairs Oversight, Health, Higher Education, and Interstate Cooperation.
Announced her candidacy for Congress in June 2025, initially challenging incumbent Rep. David Scott in the Democratic primary, and won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 56.1% of the vote.
Lived in Lilburn, Georgia, as of 2020, according to Ballotpedia.

priorities.text: Said in a campaign ad that she had "been taking on the toughest fights for Georgia families," including "against Governor Kemp and the MAGA Republicans attacking our abortion rights, our voting rights, and our health."
Campaign website says she wants "to bring a science voice to Washington."

positions.summary: Campaign website says the federal government must act to ensure access to full reproductive services, including abortions.
positions.quote: the federal government must take action to ensure that everyone who needs it has access to full reproductive services, including access to contraceptives, STI testing, cancer screenings, and abortions

positions.summary: Campaign website says Congress is overdue to raise the minimum wage so paychecks keep up with the cost of living.
positions.quote: we’re long overdue for increasing the minimum wage so paychecks keep up with the actual cost of living for working people

positions.summary: Campaign website says she would push in Congress for an assault weapon and bump stock ban, comprehensive background checks and safe storage laws.
positions.quote: I’ll push for a real assault weapon and bump stock ban, comprehensive background checks and safe storage laws

positions.summary: Campaign website calls for repealing the 2025 Trump tax cuts and making the wealthy and large corporations pay more.
positions.quote: repeal the Trump tax cuts and make the wealthy and big corporations pay their fair share

positions.summary: Campaign website, under the heading "Stop Unconstitutional ICE Raids," says she would hold the administration and ICE accountable for what she calls illegal raids and calls for transparency on where detainees are held.
positions.quote: In Congress, I vow to hold the Trump administration and ICE accountable when they illegally raid our cities and lock up our neighbors

record.text: Elected to the Georgia House of Representatives, District 108, in 2018 and re-elected in 2020, 2022, and 2024.

candidates.name: Jonathan Chavez
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed in the Republican primary

summary.text: Jonathan Chavez is the Republican nominee in Georgia's 13th District. A 23-year U.S. Air Force veteran who deployed to Iraq, he later earned degrees from the University of New Mexico, Harvard, and Johns Hopkins. He previously ran as the Republican nominee for Georgia's 4th District in 2022 and for this seat in 2024, and says he is running on transparency, fiscal responsibility, and expanded healthcare and education access.

background.text: Born in Albuquerque, New Mexico; graduated from Sandia High School.
Served in the U.S. Air Force from 1990 to 2013, including deployments to Iraq where, by his own account, he received a commendation medal.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of New Mexico in 2014, a graduate degree from Harvard University in 2019, and a graduate degree from Johns Hopkins University in 2023. He describes his Harvard and Johns Hopkins studies as focused on business, finance, and health care administration.
Lists his career experience as including work as a director, and has been affiliated with the Harvard Club of Georgia, Veterans of Foreign Wars, and Mother of God Byzantine Catholic Church.
Was the Republican nominee for Georgia's 4th District in 2022 and lost the general election to incumbent Hank Johnson.
Won the May 21, 2024 Republican primary for Georgia's 13th District over Johsie Cruz Fletcher, then lost the November general election to incumbent David Scott, 71.8% to 28.2%.
Ran unopposed in the 2026 Republican primary and is on the November 3 ballot.
Describes himself as a husband and father of four.

priorities.text: Says his campaign is about "putting our community's needs above party politics" and will "fight for more good-paying jobs, expanded healthcare options (including rural telehealth and Medicaid expansion), and better funding for our schools."
Supports term limits for members of Congress and greater accountability for federal spending.

positions.summary: Supports expanding healthcare options including rural telehealth and Medicaid expansion.
Campaign website says he supports school choice and expanding charter options.
positions.quote: empowering school choice, expanding charter options

statements.quote: Enhancing resources for police and sheriff departments

statements.context: On his campaign website (foreign policy section)

statements.quote: balanced conservation via energy independence and innovation will safeguard Georgia’s natural beauty without harming jobs

candidates.researchNotes: Statements and one position from his campaign website (jonathanchavezforcongress.com). The site does not state positions on abortion, guns, or most other tracked issues.
